text: The ADB-supported Disaster Resilience Improvement Programs (DRIP and DRIP2) in the Philippines are designed to enhance disaster risk financing through policy-based, multi-year contingent financing. These programs aim to integrate disaster risk reduction and management (DRRM) with public financial management (PFM), strengthen the role of state-owned corporations in disaster response, and introduce a city-level parametric disaster insurance scheme. The initiative addresses the Philippines' high multi-hazard risk profile by providing pre-arranged financing and integrated governance to mitigate fiscal shocks and safeguard livelihoods.
